claims.text: The baseline catalyst is an equimolar nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
The Pd fraction will be increased relative to the equimolar baseline while all other compositional and processing parameters are held constant.
Increasing the Pd fraction shifts the d-band center of Pt and adjacent active sites.
Pd enrichment alters the local electronic structure of the catalyst.
A shift in the d-band center changes the adsorption strengths of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The changed adsorption strengths alter the ethanol-oxidation reaction pathway.
The altered reaction pathway improves catalytic activity.
Pd-enriched catalysts will exhibit a measurable d-band-center shift relative to the equimolar catalyst.
The d-band-center shift can be determined by in situ XPS or UPS under ethanol-oxidation conditions.
The d-band-center shift will correlate with a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
The d-band-center shift will correlate with a higher ethanol-oxidation current density.
The hypothesis is restricted to conditions under which the nanoscale solid-solution structure is maintained and phase segregation does not occur.
Excessive Pd enrichment may induce phase separation.
Phase separation would invalidate interpretation of the intervention as controlled electronic tuning within one solid-solution phase.
Failure of increasing Pd content to produce a systematic d-band-center shift would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a corresponding improvement or predictable change in catalytic activity relative to the equimolar baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
